name: Twitter Card Validator
title: Twitter Card Validator: Preview X Cards Now
description: X retired its Card Validator. Paste a URL to preview your X card, see which tags X reads (twitter: vs og: fallbacks) and fix image errors.
answer: X's own Card Validator is no longer a practical way to preview cards, so this tool does the job: enter a URL and we fetch it as Twitterbot, check the twitter:card type and the Open Graph fallbacks, measure the image and show how the card will look on X. Most pages need just one X-specific tag.
trust: We request the page with X's Twitterbot user agent and build the preview from exactly what it receives.
body:
## Twitter Card Preview: How Your Link Looks on X

X builds a card from your page's tags when someone posts the link. The `twitter:card` tag picks the layout; title, description and image come from `twitter:` tags or, if those are missing, from Open Graph tags.

| twitter:card | Layout |
|---|---|
| summary_large_image | Large image above the link — what most sites want |
| summary | Small square thumbnail beside the text |
| player / app | Video players and app installs (special cases) |

So the minimum for a big-image card is one tag on top of your Open Graph set: `<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">`.

## X Card Validator: Fix summary_large_image Errors

Most broken cards come from four problems: no `twitter:card` tag (X falls back to a small summary at best), an image X can't fetch, an SVG image, or a page that returns an error to Twitterbot. The checker tests each one.

## What happened to the official Card Validator?

X's old validator page now sends logged-out visitors to a login screen instead of showing a preview. X's developer documentation for cards has also moved: when we checked on October 24, 2026, the old card docs URLs redirected to a general docs overview. Image requirements are now best inferred from the Open Graph standards platforms share: 1200×630 at 1.91:1 works for X, [Facebook](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/sharing/webmasters/images/) and [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a521928) alike.

## How common are X cards?

Very. In our October 2026 analysis of 315 big-brand homepages ([dataset](/resources/technical-seo-baseline-2026-10.json)), 82.5% set a `twitter:card` tag: 74.3% chose `summary_large_image` and 7.3% `summary`.

## Why does X still show my old card?

X caches cards. After you fix tags, the old preview can persist on existing posts; new posts usually pick up the change. Adding a query string such as `?v=2` to the shared URL usually makes X fetch the page again.

To see your link on six platforms at once, use the [link preview tool](/tools/link-preview). To check every og: tag in depth, use the [Open Graph checker](/tools/open-graph-checker).

faqs.q: Does X still have a Card Validator?
faqs.a: The old cards-dev.twitter.com page now sends logged-out visitors to a login screen rather than showing a preview. This tool fetches your page as Twitterbot and renders the card for anyone, no account needed.

faqs.q: Do I need twitter:title and twitter:image if I have Open Graph tags?
faqs.a: Usually not. X falls back to og:title, og:description and og:image. Add twitter: versions only when you want X to show something different from other platforms.

faqs.q: What image size works for summary_large_image?
faqs.a: A 1200×630 image at roughly 2:1 to 1.91:1 works well on X and doubles as your Open Graph image for Facebook and LinkedIn. Use PNG, JPEG or WebP, not SVG.
